newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to sell stake in oil refinery.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to sell stake in oil refinery.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski said on Friday the country's biggest oil refinery Neftochim will be offered for partial privatisation.
"Neftochim will be privatised partially," Sofianski told reporters.
Energy officials said huge investments were needed to modernise the refinery and a partial privatisation could be the key to this.

Under Bulgarian law the Privatisation Agency has to open privatisation procedures, some of which take years before selling off a state-run enterprise. The agency has not yet opened a procedure for Neftochim.
A 25-percent stake was offered for mass privatisation last year.

Neftochim, which supplies almost the whole domestic market, owes millions of dollars to crude suppliers and lacks cash to pay for crude. For the last two weeks the country has been choked by a severe petrol crisis.
Bulgaria's new interim cabinet on Thursday sacked the board of directors of Neftochim. Within two weeks the new board is due to prepare a stabilisation programme for the refinery.
Sofianski, who visited Neftochim, located at the Black Sea port of Bourgas, late on Thursday, said the interim government would seek financial stabilisation of the plant.
